subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw expose Gateway method calls to ordinary external plugins, and if so should the API be raw method dispatch, an allowlisted request surface, or typed inter-plugin service contracts?
rationale: This choice changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary; automation cannot safely choose which methods external plugins may invoke or which schemas become stable plugin contracts.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized contract
options.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep trusted-only Gateway requests
options.body: Treat current `api.runtime.gateway.request` as sufficient for bundled/trusted official plugins and decline ordinary external plugin-to-plugin dispatch for now.

options.title: Allow raw Gateway dispatch
options.body: Expose a generic method string caller and intentionally accept the larger security and compatibility surface.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current route-scoped dispatch contract and is the strongest history match for the Gateway/plugin authorization boundary.
